name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body: In addition to its standard rules, each Battle Forge scenario has two random tables that add additional Victory Point-scoring opportunities for players that vary each time the scenario is played. Mission Modifiers add additional scoring opportunities based on the position of a player’s models on the table. Achievements add additional scoring opportunities based on a player’s actions taken on the battlefield. Players should roll a d6 to randomly determine Mission Modifiers and Achievements before the beginning of a game, or players can choose them at will if all players agree. It is recommended that only one Mission Modifier and one Achievement should be in effect during any match (unless you really want to get crazy).

name: Name
body: If a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 5" x 5".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 2" x 2". Small obstacles provide cover.

name: Name
body: An elevated platform at least 1" above the table, such as a hill or terrace. Plateaus can possess multiple areas at different heights that models can be placed on, but the areas must be level to prevent models from falling over. If a model cannot be placed on a level area without risk of falling off, it cannot occupy that area. Models cannot be placed on slopes, and we recommend that plateau terrain with sloped surfaces not be used. Hill, Small—A plateau platform with a footprint approximately 6" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 30 mm models to be placed on. Hill, Large—A plateau with a footprint approximately 6" to 12" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 40 mm models to be placed on.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of rubble approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: A 3" x 5" trench template.

name: Name
body: Information is the most valuable resource one can possess during wartime, and safeguarding its delivery through a hostile combat zone is one of the greatest challenges any leader can accept. Your mission is to escort your messenger safely across the field of battle while seizing any opportunity to eliminate your adversary’s own message courier. Your nation’s position in this ongoing war depends on your success!

name: Name
body: "Kill the Messenger" is designed for 30-point and 50-point forces.

name: Name
body: "Kill the Messenger"ends after six turns.

name: Name
body: Each player has a messenger trying to get from one side of the map to the other. The messenger must check in at random points to determine a route to their destination. Only after the messenger has checked in at three locations can they exit the map and carry their message to safety.

name: Name
body: Get your messenger safely across the map and exit before your opponent does the same.

name: Name
body:
This scenario uses the map layout below. Place 9 objective markers, 2 small hills, 2 small forests, 1 medium building, 1 large pond, 4 small walls, and 2 small obstacles on the table as shown.
The objective markers are Intelligence objectives.

name: Name
body:
After determining who will go first, each player designates one of their solo or trooper models in play to be their messenger. Each player’s messenger has to check in at three Intelligence objectives before attempting to exit the table.
Before the start of the game, each player determines and secretly records which Intelligence objective in the row furthest from their deployment zone their messenger must make their third check in. Set the records aside together in a safe place. A player will only show their record to their opponent once they have checked in to this objective.
A messenger can check in to any Intelligence objective in the first or second row and must check in to Intelligence objectives in order; first an objective in the front row, then an objective in the second, and finally an objective in the third row. A messenger checks in when it ends its activation within 1" of an intelligence objective.
If your messenger is destroyed or removed from play, another solo or trooper model in your force can be designated as the messenger by checking in at the last Intelligence objective where the previous messenger checked in. If no check-in has occurred, then no check-in is required to designate a new messenger.

name: Name
body:
No points are scored when a newly designated messenger checks in at a point where the player’s previous messenger already checked in.
A player scores 1 Victory Point when their messenger checks in at the first row.
A player scores 2 Victory Points when their messenger checks in at the second row.
A player scores 3 Victory Points when their messenger checks in at the third row. Reveal your secret record at this time.
A player scores 1 Victory Point each time an attack made by a friendly model destroys or removes an enemy messenger from play.
A messenger must check in at all three rows before exiting the table. To exit the table, a messenger must end its activation within 1" of the opposing player’s table edge.

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Behind Enemy Lines—Score 1 victory point at the beginning of your turn for holding your opponent’s deployment zone. 2. Held at Bay—Beginning with the third round, score 1 Victory Point at the beginning of your turn if your opponent’s Leader is within 12" of the rear edge of their deployment zone. 3. Territory Control—Divide the table evenly into four 24" x 24" quadrants. Score 1 Victory Point for every quadrant you dominate at the beginning of your turn.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Attrition—Score 3 Victory Points when your opponent’s last Cohort model is destroyed or removed from play. 2. Bloodletting—Score 1 Victory Point the first time one of your models damages an enemy Leader with an attack each turn. 3. Exterminator—Score 1 Victory Point when you destroy or remove from play a unit with its starting number of models in a single turn.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player wins if their messenger has exited the table and their opponent’s messenger has not. If both players’ messengers have exited the table at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most victory points wins the match. Point Advantage Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with 5 or more victory points than their opponent wins the match. Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match. Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, or at the end of six rounds, the player with the most victory points wins the match.
